narrative:
The model estimates a 78% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you will leave. With over 11 years of overall experience, you are in a smaller group compared to most employees the model expects to stay, who typically have far less accumulated time in the workforce. This signals to the system that you may be ready for bigger opportunities elsewhere.

Next, the length of time you have spent in your current role also strongly influences the prediction toward leaving. At 1-5 years here, your tenure matches the most common range among those expected to stay, yet in your specific combination of factors it contributes to the model seeing higher turnover risk.

Finally, not having received other job offers while at this company pulls the prediction in the opposite direction, slightly favoring the chance you might stay. However, this positive influence is not enough to outweigh the first two factors.

The organization should consider discussing your long-term career goals with you and exploring whether additional responsibilities or growth opportunities could increase your sense of commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel like the right choice. (218 words)
